title: Block: A Queue (Deque)
oneLiner: For each call time, count the calls in the last 3000 ms by dropping old times off the front of a queue.
keyTakeaway: A queue adds at the back and removes from the front in O(1). In Python that means collections.deque and popleft, never list.pop(0), which shifts every element.
explanation:
times is increasing. For each time t, return how many times so far fall in [t - 3000, t], including t itself. [1, 100, 3001, 3002] gives [1, 2, 3, 3]: at 3002 the call at 1 has dropped out.

Push each time onto the back of a queue, then pop from the front while the front is older than t - 3000. What is left is exactly the recent window, so its length is the answer for t. C# uses Queue<int> (Enqueue, Peek, Dequeue); Python uses collections.deque (append, [0], popleft).

starterCode.python:
def recent_counts(times):
    # 1. Make an empty queue and an empty result list.
    # 2. For each time, add it to the back of the queue.
    # 3. Remove times from the front while they are older than the current time minus 3000.
    # 4. Append the queue's length to the result.
    # 5. Return the result.
    return []

gotchas: Using list.pop(0) in Python, which is O(n) per pop.
An off-by-one on the boundary: a call exactly 3000 ms ago still counts.

complexity.note: Every time is pushed once and popped at most once; the queue can hold all n times.
